scope: Baseline recognition cards for the existing 30 Threads candidates, plus opening-chapter omissions. Not a complete named-person inventory.

cards.name: Pierre Bezukhov
cards.body: The illegitimate son of the wealthy Count Bezukhov. A young man recently returned to Russia after being educated abroad.

cards.name: Prince Andrei Bolkonski
cards.body: Marya’s brother and Lise’s husband. An officer serving as Kutuzov’s aide.

cards.name: Natasha Rostova
cards.body: The Rostovs’ younger daughter; sister of Nikolai, Vera, and Petya.

cards.name: Nikolai Rostov
cards.body: The Rostovs’ elder son; brother of Natasha, Vera, and Petya.

cards.name: Princess Marya Bolkonskaya
cards.body: Old Prince Bolkonski’s daughter and Andrei’s sister. She lives with her father at Bald Hills.

cards.name: Old Prince Bolkonski
cards.body: A wealthy, retired army officer. Father of Andrei and Marya.

cards.name: Hélène Kuragina
cards.body: Prince Vasili’s daughter, admired for her beauty. Sister of Hippolyte and Anatole.

cards.name: Prince Vasili Kuragin
cards.body: An influential courtier. Father of Hélène, Hippolyte, and Anatole.

cards.name: Anatole Kuragin
cards.body: Prince Vasili’s younger son; brother of Hélène and Hippolyte.

cards.name: Count Ilya Rostov
cards.body: The father of Nikolai, Natasha, Vera, and Petya. Head of the hospitable Rostov household in Moscow.

cards.name: Countess Rostova
cards.body: Count Ilya Rostov’s wife and the mother of Nikolai, Natasha, Vera, and Petya.

cards.name: Petya Rostov
cards.body: The youngest Rostov child; brother of Nikolai, Natasha, and Vera.

cards.name: Sonya
cards.body: The Rostov children’s cousin, brought up in their household.

cards.name: Vera Rostova
cards.body: The Rostovs’ elder daughter; sister of Nikolai, Natasha, and Petya.

cards.name: Fyodor Dolokhov
cards.body: An officer in Anatole Kuragin’s circle, known for his daring.

cards.name: Vasily Denisov
cards.body: A cavalry captain in the Pavlograd Hussars and Nikolai Rostov’s squadron commander. Also called Vaska.

cards.name: Boris Drubetskoy
cards.body: Anna Mikhaylovna Drubetskaya’s son. A young man whose mother seeks help securing his military career.

cards.name: Anna Pavlovna Scherer
cards.body: The St. Petersburg hostess; a lady-in-waiting and favorite of the Dowager Empress.

cards.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
cards.body: The French emperor, also called Buonaparte.

cards.name: Kutuzov
cards.body: A Russian general. Andrei Bolkonski serves as his aide.

cards.name: Emperor Alexander I
cards.body: Russia’s reigning emperor.

cards.name: Prince Bagration
cards.body: A Russian general commanding troops in the campaign against Napoleon.

cards.name: Captain Tushin
cards.body: A Russian artillery officer who commands a battery of guns.

cards.name: Platon Karataev
cards.body: A Russian soldier from a peasant background, held prisoner alongside Pierre.

cards.name: Berg
cards.body: A young officer acquainted with the Rostov family.

cards.name: Julie Karagina
cards.body: A young woman in the Rostovs’ social circle; daughter of Marya Lvovna Karagina.

cards.name: Mademoiselle Bourienne
cards.body: Princess Marya’s French companion at Bald Hills.

cards.name: Tikhon Shcherbaty
cards.body: A peasant serving with Denisov’s partisan detachment.

cards.name: Balashev
cards.body: A Russian general and trusted aide to Emperor Alexander.

cards.name: Bilibin
cards.body: A Russian diplomat acquainted with Andrei Bolkonski.

cards.name: Hippolyte Kuragin
cards.body: Prince Vasili’s elder son; brother of Hélène and Anatole.

cards.name: Lise Bolkonskaya
cards.body: Andrei’s wife, also called Lise Meinen, her maiden name.

cards.name: Vicomte de Mortemart
cards.body: A French aristocrat living abroad, invited to Anna Pavlovna’s gathering.

cards.name: Abbé Morio
cards.body: A clergyman and thinker invited to Anna Pavlovna’s gathering.

cards.name: Baron Funke
cards.body: A candidate for a diplomatic post in Vienna, supported by the Dowager Empress.

cards.name: Empress Marya Fedorovna
cards.body: The Dowager Empress and Anna Pavlovna’s patroness. “Dowager” means the widow of an emperor.

cards.name: Novosiltsev
cards.body: A Russian envoy involved in the negotiations with England discussed at Anna Pavlovna’s gathering.

cards.name: Hardenberg
cards.body: A Prussian statesman. His name is spelled “Hardenburg” in the older English edition.

cards.name: Haugwitz
cards.body: A Prussian statesman mentioned alongside Hardenberg.

cards.name: Wintzingerode
cards.body: An envoy mentioned in connection with seeking Prussia’s support.

cards.name: The King of Prussia
cards.body: The Prussian monarch whose support Russia is seeking.

cards.name: Lavater
cards.body: A writer known for trying to read character from physical appearance. Vasili invokes him in a joke about fatherhood.

cards.name: The Bonapartes
cards.body: Napoleon Bonaparte’s family.

cards.name: The Montmorencys
cards.body: A French aristocratic family connected with Mortemart.

cards.name: The Rohans
cards.body: A French aristocratic family cited among Mortemart’s connections.

requiredReview: The initial source worksheet exposes wrong owners: Count Bezukhov is Pierre’s father; Marya may be the Empress; Countess Rostova may be Natasha’s mother; Petya may address Pierre; Tikhon may be the Bolkonski servant rather than Shcherbaty. Do not import Threads aliases as runtime bindings.
Supply original/modern edition display variants, including Andrew/Andrei and Mary/Marya.
Add missing people throughout the novel, including Anna Mikhaylovna, Count Kirill Bezukhov, and the separate servant Tikhon. The 30 Threads candidates are not a complete cast.
Review category release gates independently from identity copy. Karataev and Shcherbaty must not appear before their actual encounters.
Review later identity changes selectively. A spouse dying or a military appointment ending may make a previously correct present-tense card misleading; do not substitute a running plot summary.
